start.text:
Backlund again, and a fourth name: Dwayne Dantès, gentleman, of independent means, who takes a box at the opera and is seen at the right dinners and has never once been photographed.

Sherlock Moriarty still has rooms on Minsk Street. Gehrman Sparrow still has a reputation in the Archipelago. Klein Moretti still has a stone in Tingen with the wrong date on it.

Four men, one coat, and the coat is getting tight.

Saint Samuel Cathedral keeps the Antigonus family’s notebook behind the Chanis Gate, which is not a gate and is not in the cathedral, exactly, and which the Church does not discuss.

You have four names, a Marionettist’s threads, and eleven minutes while the choir is between settings.

check.text:
It is not a lock and it is not a ward. It is Sealed Artifact 0-17, and it does not keep people out of the vault.

It keeps them somewhere else instead. Which is a different profession entirely, and a much older one.

in.text:
You get as far as the inner arch, and the theft fails.

It does not fail because you were caught, or slow, or wrong about the choir. It fails because the Chanis Gate is not a door in a wall — and the floor of Saint Samuel Cathedral stops being the floor of Saint Samuel Cathedral while your second foot is still coming down.

start.text:
A town. Cobbles, shutters, a market cross, a clock.

No people. No wind. No sound that you did not make, and a four-hundred-year-old fog standing between the houses at the exact height of a man’s shoulders.

Sealed Artifact 0-17 does not keep thieves out of the vault. It keeps them here.

The town clock is stopped at a time that is not on any dial you have seen — a thirteenth hour, cut into the face by the man who made it, deliberately, as a joke or a warning.

It is still warm. Four hundred years stopped, and still warm.

hand.text:
Time here is not passing. It is being held, the way a note is held, by something that has been holding it since before Loen had a name for itself.

Amon. The Angel of Time, of the Error pathway. Not present, not watching — simply the reason the clock is warm, the way a fire is the reason a room is.

start.text:
‘You are the fourth,’ says the gentleman behind the counter of a shop with no stock. ‘The other three were also very confident about the choir.’

He has one initial in the Church’s file, three photographs of other men, and a note advising against arrest. The Numinous Episcopate does not put a second name on anybody it expects to keep.

choices.text: Ask what he is doing here.

why.text: ‘Waiting.’ He is entirely pleasant about it. ‘This is the only room in the world where nothing ages, and my Church has a use for a man who does not age. I am the stock. That is the joke, and I have had four hundred years to find it funny, and I have not.’

fight.text:
It takes a long time, because nothing here ages and nothing here tires, and in the end it is not strength that ends it but the fact that you are the only one of the two of you who has anywhere else to be.

Mr. A stops. The shop stays empty. The fog does not react at all.

start.text:
Not a grave. A seal cut in the shape of a grave, and under it an old man in a black hooded robe with a long white beard and eyes like water that has never had light in it.

‘You are not one of theirs,’ he says. It is not a question. ‘Four hundred years and the first one through the gate who is not one of theirs.’

who.text:
‘Zaratul.’ He says it the way a man says a name he has not needed for a while. ‘I opened a door I should not have opened, and something on the other side of it agreed with me, and the Church put me in a town where nothing happens so that the agreement could not be acted on.’

A pause. ‘I am aware of how that sounds. It is the most honest description available.’

leave.text:
You leave it, and get halfway across the square, and understand that the way out of a place where nothing happens is held open by something that has been trying to make something happen for four hundred years.

You go back.

break.text:
You break it, and the fog moves for the first time since the fourteenth century, and the way out opens because he opens it.

‘A favour,’ says Zaratul, from somewhere behind you and already a long way off. ‘I am very good at gratitude. You will find out how good, and you will not enjoy the finding out, and neither of those facts makes this a mistake.’

out.text:
Saint Samuel Cathedral, the north transept, between settings.

And for one second on the way through, something enormous and entirely patient looks at you — not the Gate, not Amon, but the Evernight Goddess herself, in her own house, watching a dead man from Tingen come back out of a place He put people.

She lets you go. You will spend a long time being unsure whether that was mercy or filing.

start.text:
Leonard Mitchell has been three months getting here and he arrives at it all at once.

‘Gehrman Sparrow is Sherlock Moriarty. Sherlock Moriarty knows things about Tingen that were never printed. And Klein Moretti is buried in Tingen.’ He looks at his own hands. ‘So I went and dug him up.’

nothing.text: He waits. He is the fastest man on any team at noticing a thing nobody wanted noticed, and he has just noticed that Dwayne Dantès is not going to help him.

found.text:
‘A coffin with a body in it.’ A beat. ‘With a body in it that is not him, and that the Church signed for, and that has been in the ground since September in a parish that does not make that kind of mistake.’

He is not accusing you. He is asking you to make it stop being his problem.

choices.text: Tell him Klein was resurrected, and serves the Fool.
Tell him nothing and let him decide.

fool.text:
You give him a version with three true sentences in it: that Klein Moretti died in the chapel, that he did not stay dead, and that what he answers to now sits above a grey fog at a bronze table.

Leonard takes it. Not because it is convincing — because it is the first explanation in three months that lets him stop digging.

decide.text:
He decides, in the end, that a man who was murdered by a deacon of a dead Order is owed the benefit of the doubt, and that he will stop asking.

He will not stop asking. He will stop saying that he is asking, which is a different service and one you can work with.

start.text:
The Southern Continent, and off it an island with a ruin on it that predates every calendar anyone still uses.

Amon has come to Backlund, which makes Backlund a place not to be. A Red Glove team is here hunting the Numinous Episcopate, and two of the people on it buried you.
The altar is older than the Church that is not here. Carved into it, a sun with its face scratched out — not weathered, scratched, by somebody who could reach and who took their time.

read.text:
The Ancient Sun God did not fall in battle.

He was let fall. The betrayal is cut into the stone in a hand that was present for it, and the names in it are names that four modern Churches teach as founders.

And there is a son. There is a son who was there, and who has been Angel of Time ever since, and who has spent four hundred years putting threads of himself into small black notebooks and letting the threads do the living.

start.text:
Alger Wilson has been on this island four days longer than he told anyone, and has been reading the two markers the whole time.

‘Facing each other,’ he says. ‘Nobody buries anybody facing anybody. These are not graves, Mr. Sparrow. These are two halves of a signature.’

signs.text:
‘An agreement.’ He does not sit back, even here, even on a rock. ‘Between the ones who did it and the one who let them. Four days apart, because the second party wanted to be seen to have thought about it.’

He looks at you with a sailor’s flat patience.

‘I have been paying the Fool for information for two years. This is the first thing I have found that I would rather he did not know, and I am going to tell him anyway, and I would like it noted that I noticed myself doing it.’

start.text:
Four tents and a wireless set that should not work at this latitude, and a Red Glove team out of Backlund hunting the Numinous Episcopate across a continent that does not want any of them.

Leonard Mitchell. Daly Simone. And, arriving on the fifth night with a folded cloth and no appetite for any of it, a deacon of an Order everyone agrees is finished.

zangwill.text:
He has come to exorcise the Red Angel evil spirit, because that is what he does now: he goes where the ingredients are, and he is patient, and he folds the cloth.

He does not recognise you. There is no reason he should. The man he shot through the heart in September is dead and the Church signed for the body.

take.text:
It takes all three of you and it costs one.

Daly Simone goes into it knowing the arithmetic — she is a Spirit Medium and the whole of her pathway is a negotiation with the dead, and she spends the last of hers holding him still for four seconds.

Leonard puts him down. You put the bullet in. Between the two of you it is not revenge and it is not justice; it is a fortnight’s work finished on a rock in the south, and a woman on the ground who was twenty-six.

after.text:
Afterwards you sit with Leonard, who does not speak for two hours, and then says: ‘She knew him from Tingen. She was at the chapel.’

Saint Selena’s ashes are in a bag on a dead man on a rock in the Southern Continent, four hundred and one days after they were taken out of a silver casket in a chapel in Tingen by a man who folded the cloth first.

start.text:
Daly Simone wears the hood and the blue eyeshadow because she is twenty-six and needs the Nighthawks who report to her to stop counting.

‘You were in Tingen,’ she says. ‘Not you. The way you stand. Somebody I knew stood like that and he is dead, so I have decided to find it restful rather than upsetting.’

choices.text: Ask what she remembers of the chapel.

chapel.text: ‘Eleven minutes underground and a clerk dead upstairs.’ She says it flatly. ‘I have been on four teams since and none of them has been told what was taken, and I have stopped asking, because the asking is what got the clerk killed.’

rest.text: She finds it restful. It costs you nothing and it is, you are aware, the last uncomplicated conversation she is going to have.

start.text: ‘Mr. Sparrow.’ Alger Wilson gives no sign at all that he has ever heard the name Fool. ‘I am here for the Church of Storms and you are here for yourself, and I would like us both to keep saying that out loud until it stops being funny.’

agree.text:
You agree. He accepts the agreement in the manner of a man filing a receipt.

It occurs to you, watching him not sit back on a rock in the Southern Continent, that Mr. Hanged Man has been paying the Fool for two years, and has never once asked the Fool for anything he could not have got elsewhere at a worse price.

He is not buying information. He is establishing that he is a customer, against a day when he will need to be more than one.
